newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Swedish jet crashed on practice attack.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Swedish jet crashed on practice attack.

text.p: A senior Russian naval official said on Friday that a Swedish jet which crashed into the sea just metres from a Russian nuclear-powered warship earlier this week had just carried out a dummy attack on the vessel.
The Viggen jet flew low over the Russian cruiser Pyotr Veliky on Wednesday before ploughing into the Baltic Sea, killing the pilot.

The Swedes said the jet was on a surveillance mission. But Interfax news agency quoted Igor Kasatonov, first deputy commander of the Russian navy, as saying the pilot had been carrying out a practice attack.
"Such attacks, which have also been carried out on Russian ships in the past, are a violation of all international norms," the agency quoted him as saying.
It seemed clear from the context of his quotes that he was referring to alleged practice attacks on Russian ships around the world and not just by the Swedes.
Russian navy officials said the Viggen flew over the ship and crashed when the pilot lost control of the plane as he tried to make a sharp right-hand turn at low altitude.

But the head of Sweden's air force said the crashed jet had been trying to avoid a Russian submarine reconnaissance airplane in the vicinity. The Viggen hit the water about 120 km (75 miles) off the southeast coast of Sweden.
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said the Pyotr Veliky had been en route from St Petersburg to the port of Baltiisk in the western Russian enclave of Kaliningrad when the crash occurred.
